observations: The authoritative direct current failure is real_tool.case_axi_ddr_interface. Its report rejects simulation.source_identity_sha256, Vivado-export compile_authority, ordered-command authority_refs, and simulator executable authorization because they do not bind the current exact sample-project identity and export facts.

The current functional-simulation precondition also lacks the required exact_sample_top_module loader token. This is a board testbench loader/binding defect; it does not authorize changing the immutable semantic testbench contract, stimulus, expected outputs, numeric policy, wrapper sources, or DUT RTL.

real_tool.case_vcs_functional_sim and the downstream board gates were not run because case_axi_ddr_interface failed. Their not_run states and the missing board semantic report are evidence gaps or dependency cascades, not independent RTL, AXI, DDR, value, order, numeric, or liveness failures.

The current debug closure classifies the failure as a verification_semantic_capability_contract gap and has no current localized boundary, root candidate, or lower-layer challenge. Therefore the identity/harness capability must be repaired before obtaining a hardware boundary trace.

The operator-leaf and connected single-layer gates have live hash-validated promotion certificates. The lower-layer challenge status is no_lower_layer_challenge, so those layers must remain closed. Any later board trace must show current direct core start, ingress, egress, a named causal boundary, and certificate-hash contradiction before lower-layer revalidation may be scheduled.

The connected kernel is certified as an elastic, variable-latency token pipeline. Required boundary order and adjacent-stage cross-token overlap must be preserved; unequal stage durations or absence of strict same-cycle start/end are not failures by themselves.

The prior repair feedback contains a nonterminal VCS trace and runner-termination ambiguity. Because the current VCS invocation is dependency-skipped and the supplied diagnosis applicability is historical_only after a live source hash change, that evidence may guide termination instrumentation but cannot justify a current source repair or hardware claim.
The conditional design-team review was no_split and supplied no specialist action or deterministic evidence that changes the primary repair-agent decision.

sacg_memory_truth reports 15 active current-scope contamination barriers and six open retry requests, including retry_request.0136, retry_request.0140, retry_request.0141, retry_request.0142, retry_request.0143, and retry_request.0144. They block downstream trust and promotion until checker-validated superseding artifacts are produced. There is no open current-scope backtrack request.

A board functional pass must continue to bind the complete target-checkpoint tensor catalog, immutable input provenance, independent target-model Transformer-block outputs for the same checkpoint/input, frozen numeric tolerances, semantic testbench hashes, exact wrapper hashes, and executed proof that the DUT consumed every required Transformer-block tensor.
proposed_actions: Repair only the current board-simulation identity, compile-authority, executable-provenance, and existing testbench-loader bindings from current exact sample-project discovery and Vivado evidence; rerun the failed AXI/DDR interface checker.

Add runner-side terminal-evidence capture so a replay records the raw simulator termination event, external kill indication, wall-time budget, cycle budget, and authorization status. Do not alter RTL to compensate for incomplete execution.

After the static interface gate passes, replay the exact board-wrapped system with unchanged checkpoint, stimulus, target reference, numeric policy, testbench contract, wrapper hashes, and required weight bindings; collect current boundary and frontier traces.

If the replay fails with simulator-side evidence, localize the earliest violated current-layer boundary or integration contract before proposing any code repair. If execution is externally truncated, repair or approve the runner budget and replay unchanged.

Only after the replay and all remaining board-layer gates pass, assemble board semantic evidence and publish a superseding Stage7 result; then reconcile the six open retry requests and 15 active barriers through SACG checkers.
risks: Using a stale identity hash, guessed top module, uncited Vivado export context, reordered compile command, or unauthorized simulator executable could compile a different board design while appearing to exercise the sample project.
Changing the board testbench semantics or wrapper source merely to satisfy the missing loader token would violate the immutable repair contract and invalidate prior and future comparison evidence.

A repeated nonterminal remote VCS run could again yield missing monitor and semantic reports. Without the raw termination marker and configured wall-time/cycle budget, an environmental kill cannot be distinguished from a simulator-side liveness failure.

Independent AXI reads, prefetch activity, or accepted later inputs do not prove output/lifecycle-frontier progress. Conversely, a frontier stall is localization evidence, not a preselected scheduler, wrapper, memory, or connected-kernel root cause.

Reopening leaf or connected-kernel RTL based only on a downstream board output symptom would discard certified model, shape, numeric, ordering, and elastic-pipeline invariants without a current contradiction.

Board-level shape, token order, address map, transfer count, tensor layout, and runtime lifecycle consistency remain unproven until an authorized current simulation executes and its monitors complete.

Weight files on disk are insufficient. Missing complete-scope tensor hashes, loader binding, or executed DUT-consumption evidence must remain a verification-capability blocker rather than being treated as hardware correctness.

Generating expected outputs randomly, from RTL output, or through an identity/default model would contaminate numeric acceptance. The existing independent target-model contract and tolerance must remain frozen.
Historical Stage7, Stage8, diagnosis, and trace artifacts covered by active contamination barriers are planning evidence only and cannot support backend or board-runtime promotion.
No implementation or backend evidence is relevant yet; proceeding to synthesis, implementation, bitstream, or runtime release would skip the failed third-layer repair loop.

constraints: Repair the board-layer verification capability before requesting hardware-boundary diagnosis.
Use the exact user-supplied sample-project wrapper and current source hashes; do not substitute a simplified wrapper.
Do not reopen certified lower layers without a current hash-bound trace directly contradicting a named invariant.
Preserve elastic variable-latency connected-kernel ordering and required cross-token overlap; same-cycle stage completion is not required.
Keep checkpoint, stimulus, independent target-model reference, resolved numeric policy and tolerance, semantic testbench contract, and exact wrapper hashes immutable.
Expected outputs must come from the target model on the same checkpoint and stimulus, never from random data or DUT output.
Require complete tensor catalog hashes, a bound loader/harness, and executed consumption proof for every Transformer-block tensor required by the DUT.
Exclude embedding/tokenization, final model norm, LM head/logits, and sampling from DUT golden and weight-consumption scope.
No backend synthesis, implementation, bitstream, runtime-ABI release, or board runtime promotion until every board_axi_ddr_wrapped_system gate passes.
